Sean Bolling. Good afternoon, Commissioners. So I'd like to start off by reading a letter that I submitted on behalf of Detective McClafferty. On April 16, 2025, officers responded to 27 North Hill Street and reported a man finding dead. The victim was determined to have died from a fentanyl overdose. Detective John McClafferty was assigned to the investigation and through diligent investigative efforts identified Elvin Villa of Bronx, New York, as the individual responsible for supplying narcotics to Claude McClafferty's death. After exhausting local investigative leads, Detective McClafferty demonstrated exceptional initiative by disseminating this information through law enforcement channels, resulting in contact with the Fort Chester Police Department, which was investigating the fatal overdose involving the same suspect. Detective McClafferty subsequently partnered with investigators from the Fort Chester Police Department and the New York Tribal Enforcement Administration, forming a multi-agency investigation that begins narcotics trafficking operations. As the investigation progressed, the third fatal overdose in Fort Chester was also linked to the victim. Through Detective McClafferty's investigative efforts and collaboration with federal and local law enforcement, sufficient evidence was developed to obtain a federal arrest warrant and a federal search warrant for Villa and his residence. On June 4, 2026, investigators executed the federal search warrant, recovering a firearm, currency, narcotics, packaging materials, and a stamp marker matching the stamp found on the glassine fold recovered from the stamped victim's residence. The evidence directly linked Villa to the fatal overdose investigation. Villa was taken into custody and charged federally with one count of conspiring to commit narcotics trafficking resulting in a death and three counts of narcotics trafficking resulting in death. He was demanded federal custody following arraignment of each trafficking resulting in death. The charge carries a mandatory minimum sentence of 20 years in prison. John's determination, investigative skill, and ability to build effective partnerships across multiple jurisdictions directly led to the identification, apprehension, and federal prosecution of narcotics traffickers responsible for multiple fatal overdoses. His professionalism, perseverance, and unwavering commitment to justice reflect great credit upon himself, the Major Crimes Unit, and the Sanford Police Department. It is therefore respectfully requested that this letter of commendation be forwarded to the chain of command for consideration for the detective's behalf and for the Sanford Police Commissioner's award.
